newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bufete hit by receivables doubts.
newsitem.headline: Bufete hit by receivables doubts.

text.p: Shares listed by Mexican construction firm Bufete Industrial were sharply down in late trade on the Mexican bourse on Monday.
Analysts said Bufete CPO shares were down 3.20 pesos to 52 pesos on fears the company would not receive payments negotiated with the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE).
"There is a rumor in Europe the CFE will not pay Bufete out of political motives due to the new line-up in the Mexican Congress," an analyst said, who asked not to be named.
Ben Uglow of Robert Flemings Research in New York said Bufete had informed the investor public the CFE accounted for one-third of its accounts receivable.
"An important element (in explaining how the share price has fallen) is lack of confidence in the CFE business," Uglow said.
Bufete's second quarter earnings report released on Friday listed accounts receivable for work performed more than two years ago on the electricity generating projects Carbon II and Topolobampo.
